title: Scroll-button directions
blurb: Tests physical vs logical ::scroll-button() arguments in Element.pseudo(), wildcard and invalid keywords, and RTL coordinate mapping against browser-created event.pseudoTarget clicks.
question: Does Element.pseudo('::scroll-button(<dir>)') preserve author-supplied physical directions while event.pseudoTarget normalizes clicks to logical directions under LTR and RTL?
result: In Chrome 158 with the flag, pseudo('::scroll-button(left)') returns an object whose selectorText is '::scroll-button(inline-start)': physical arguments are mapped to logical names, contrary to CSSWG #14528. Browser-created event.pseudoTarget is logical in LTR and RTL (left arrow inline-start, right arrow inline-end with this page's physical anchors).
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless) with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on 2026-11-28; earlier Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12

friction.summary: Accessing ::scroll-button() as a CSSPseudoElement with selectorText requires two separate experimental flags (CSSPseudoElementSelectorText and CSSPseudoElementScrollButton)
friction.repro: Call scroller.pseudo('::scroll-button(inline-start)') in Chrome 153 without CSSPseudoElementScrollButton; it returns null even though the CSS ::scroll-button() UI renders and scrolls.
friction.workaround: Check for a non-null return from element.pseudo('::scroll-button(...)') and provide native HTML Previous/Next buttons for keyboard and production carousel navigation.

friction.summary: Author-created pseudo('::scroll-button(left)') keeps physical direction names while browser-created event.pseudoTarget always serializes logical names
friction.repro: Per CSSWG #14528, compare scroller.pseudo('::scroll-button(left)').selectorText against event.pseudoTarget.selectorText when clicking the left button in LTR or RTL.
friction.workaround: Match browser-created event.pseudoTarget.selectorText against logical keywords (inline-start, inline-end, block-start, block-end) rather than physical left/right.

friction.summary: Chrome 158 maps physical ::scroll-button() arguments to logical names in selectorText for user-created objects
friction.workaround: Compare against logical names for both user-created and browser-created objects.
